rows.title: Policy
rows.read: Almost every major central bank is leaning toward raising rates because high oil keeps inflation up. Hikes look near-certain soon in Britain, Canada and New Zealand, and likely by December in the US, the euro area and Japan. Switzerland is the odd one out, where a cut is still possible.
rows.figure: BoE Nov 5 hike ~95–99%, Dec ~51%; BoC Oct 28 ~93%; RBNZ Oct 28 ~98%; RBA Nov 3 ~42%; Fed Oct hold ~85%, Dec hike ~90%; ECB Dec ~76%; BoJ Dec ~80%

rows.title: Growth
rows.read: Growth is holding up but softening at the edges, with housing weak in the US and UK under high borrowing costs. That has not yet changed any central bank's plans, so it is not driving currencies for now.
rows.figure: UK house prices +0.9% y/y (Aug); US pending home sales −7.3% (Sep); Japan Sep exports +16.7% y/y (~+20% fc)

rows.title: Inflation
rows.read: Inflation is running hot almost everywhere because of energy, which is why so many central banks are leaning toward hikes. New Zealand's figures overnight cooled slightly but stayed above target, so they did not change the picture. Japan's inflation figures tonight matter most for the yen.
rows.figure: NZ Q3 CPI 3.7% y/y (3.8% fc; 4.1% prior); UK CPI Sep 3.5% y/y (3.4% fc); German PPI +6.7% y/y; Japan core CPI fc 2.1%, Thu 6:30 PM CT

rows.title: Risk
rows.read: The Gulf conflict moved closer to Saudi oil sites, and the US told some diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia. Markets took it calmly: safe havens like the yen, franc and gold saw no rush of buying. In Europe, the stress point remains France's high borrowing costs.

rows.title: Terms of trade
rows.read: Oil is back near its recent highs on the risk of attacks reaching Saudi supply. That helps exporters like Canada and hurts big energy importers like Japan and the euro area. Australia and New Zealand also benefit from firm prices for what they sell abroad.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.read: Hedge funds are betting most heavily against the Canadian dollar, even as a Bank of Canada hike looks likely, which leaves those bets exposed if the loonie keeps rising. They also bet against the kiwi and the euro. In the yen and the Aussie, hedge funds and long-term investors take opposite sides.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.read: Government finances are weighing on the euro, with France's borrowing costs at their highest in over twenty years before a credit rating review on Friday. In Britain, the October 28 budget comes next and may add help with energy bills.
rows.figure: France 10-year >5%; Moody's on France Fri Oct 23 (Aa3, negative outlook); French revenue vote Oct 27; UK Sep borrowing £24.5bn (£23.9bn fc); UK budget Oct 28
